title: Second commandment (CCC 2142–2159)
hook: the holy name, and your own name too

segments.voice: Yesterday, the first commandment: faith, hope and love aimed at God, and no luck charm in his place. Your line was god first. Did you set down one small superstition? Day one thousand one hundred twenty-five.

The coffee shop is loud. The barista slides a cup across the counter and calls out a name that's almost yours, spelled the way no one has ever spelled it. You take the cup anyway. Later that week, at a funeral, a grandson reads his grandmother's full name aloud, every part of it, slowly, and the room goes still. Same thing, a name. In one place, scribbled and forgotten. In the other, held like something precious. Today's commandment is about a name, God's, and it ends up being about yours.
screen: `A NAME MISSPELLED ON A CUP.` → `A FULL NAME READ AT A FUNERAL.` → `GOD'S NAME, AND YOURS.`

segments.voice: In Exodus, in the Douay-Rheims: "Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain." The Catechism begins with a gift. It says God entrusts his name to those who believe in him. In Exodus, God tells Moses his name at the burning bush. To give someone your name is to let them call on you. So the commandment asks for respect, the way you'd guard the name of someone you love. The Catechism names what goes against it. Blasphemy: words of hatred or contempt aimed at God, at the Church, at the saints. Using God's name to cover crimes, or to justify violence against a people. Careless swearing, where the holiest name becomes filler. And a false oath: calling on God as witness to a lie. Jesus, in the Sermon on the Mount, goes further and tells his followers not to swear at all, but to let their yes mean yes. The Catechism notes the Church still allows an oath for a serious and just reason, like testimony in court. Then comes a turn. The Catechism moves from God's name to the listener's. In baptism, it says, a person is baptized in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and receives their own name in the Church. God calls each one by name, it says, and everyone's name is sacred. The Catechism calls a name the icon of the person: it deserves respect as a sign of the dignity of the one who bears it. In the book of Revelation, the one who overcomes is promised a white stone with a new name written on it, which no one knows but the one who receives it. So the second commandment guards two names at once: the name above every name, and the one on your coffee cup.
screen: `GOD ENTRUSTS HIS NAME.` · `NOT IN VAIN: BLASPHEMY, FALSE OATHS.` · `GOD CALLS EACH ONE BY NAME.` · `A WHITE STONE, A NEW NAME.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: use God's name only with love. Settle, and breathe. If you pray, say God's name once, slowly, the way you'd say the name of someone you trust, and let the silence after it be long. If you don't pray, say instead the name of someone you love, just as slowly, and notice how a name carries a whole person. Then say your own name, quietly, as though someone kind were saying it to you. The bell holds the time.
Second commandment. Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain: respect for God's name, and, the Catechism adds, for every person's name. Today's word.
Your line: names are holy. Today, learn the name of someone you see often but have never asked, and use it. Day one thousand one hundred twenty-five.

howItsDone: Catholics are taught to speak God's name with reverence; at baptism a child receives a Christian name, which may be a saint's, and the priest baptizes in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.

match.prompt: the second commandment — tap the pairs.
pairs: words of contempt aimed at God
calling God to witness a lie
receiving your name in the Church
a new name, known to the receiver

myth: the second commandment is only about swearing
the Catechism also covers blasphemy, oaths, and the dignity of every person's name.
the Catechism calls a person's name sacred
it calls a name the icon of the person.
the Church forbids every oath, even in court
the Catechism allows an oath for a serious and just reason.

fork.setup: you're asked to swear before God that something is true, and it's a small lie that would spare everyone trouble. what does the second commandment say?
options: never call God to witness a lie.
fork.reveal: the Catechism says a false oath calls on God to be witness to a lie, and calls perjury a grave lack of respect for the Lord of all speech.

trapdoor: what you thought: don't curse using God's name.
what it means: respect God's name, keep your oaths true, and honor every person's name as sacred.
what a scholar hears: God entrusting his name at the bush, the Catechism's 'icon of the person', and the white stone of Revelation 2:17.
recall: a firm habit of doing good

sources.quoted: Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain.

notes: CCC 2142–2159 paraphrased (copyrighted translation). 'Icon of the person' follows CCC 2158; 'everyone's name is sacred' follows CCC 2158; oath for a serious and just reason follows CCC 2154.
'Using God's name to cover crimes, or to justify violence against a people' paraphrases CCC 2148; confirm wording.
Fork reveal follows CCC 2151 (a false oath calls on God to be witness to a lie) and CCC 2152 (perjury is a grave lack of respect for the Lord of all speech); confirm.
Exodus 20:7 quoted from Douay-Rheims; confirm exact wording.
Isaiah 43:1 ('called thee by thy name') deliberately not quoted; CCC 2158 cites it and a Keeper may wish to add it in Douay-Rheims.
howItsDone: 'which may be a saint's'; CCC 2156 says the name can be a saint's. Confirm phrasing.

Editor pass 2: 'the name above every name' (Philippians 2:9, paraphrased) now cited in sources; howItsDone's frequency claim 'often a saint's' softened; the 'warmer than a ban' opening of the teach replaced, since several nearby days used the same not-a-rule-but turn.

Audit (y4 1122–1131): fork reveal no longer says 'God, who is truth itself', which the cited paragraphs don't say in those words; it now follows CCC 2151–2152. Scripture, CCC paraphrases and the Revelation 2:17 detail checked and found sound.
